ksp-molar-solubility.alt: Three panels. A 1 to 1 salt, AgCl, dissolves to Ag+ and Cl−, each at concentration s, so Ksp = s squared and s is the square root of Ksp, 1.3 times 10 to the minus 5 M. A 1 to 2 salt, CaF2, dissolves to Ca2+ at s and F− at 2s, so Ksp = s times (2s) squared = 4s cubed and s is the cube root of Ksp over 4, 2.1 times 10 to the minus 4 M. A warning panel: square the whole 2s, compare Ksp values only for salts with the same ion ratio, and never include the solid. CaF2 has the smaller Ksp but the larger molar solubility.
